PII-scrubber CI gate asserts no tenant-identifier strings slip into old/new values |\n32\t| `observability.emergency_overrides` (Phase 8 `aqua-ctl`)    | n/a                                  | ≥ 7 years (CC7.1 incident evidence) | **7 years**                               | Emergency override is incident-class; quarterly SRE review                                                        |\n33\t| `apps/*/src/database/migrations/_archive/`                  | n/a                                  | ≥ 7 years                           | **7 years**                               | git-LFS + S3 Glacier (cost-effective cold storage); KVKK residency at FRA1 (ADR-024 cross-references R4 of plan)                  |\n35\t| `docs/reviews/_registry/findings.jsonl`                     | minimise                             | ≥ 7 years (audit trail)             | **7 years + hash-chain + PII-scrub gate** | Append-only; cryptographic integrity; CI gate prevents PII leakage into audit log                                 |\n36\t| `observability.migration_backfill_progress` (Phase 3.5)     | minimise                             | n/a                                 | **90 days after backfill completes**      | Operational/resumability data; stale rows serve no purpose                                                        |\n37\t| `s3://aqua-deploy-artifacts-fra1/spaces-access-logs/` (R36) | minimise                             | n/a                                 | **1 year**                                | Forensics window for snapshot access                                                                              |\n38\t\n39\t### PII-scrubber gate for `findings.jsonl`\n40\t\n41\t`tools/gates/findings-pii-scan.ts` — CI gate scans every new registry entry for:\n42\t\n43\t- Email address regex\n44\t- Phone number regex (E.164 + Turkish formats)\n45\t- Turkish TC Kimlik No regex (11-digit validation algorithm)\n46\t- IBAN regex\n47\t- Credit card (PAN) regex\n48\t\n49\tOn match: PR fails with pointer to the leaking field; author must redact or use HMAC reference.\n50\t\n51\t### Implementation notes\n52\t\n53\t- `migration_events` partitioning: monthly via TimescaleDB retention policy `SELECT\n54\tadd_retention_policy('migration_events', INTERVAL '13 months')`\n55\t- `schema_object_history` 7y retention: pg_cron job monthly moves rows older than 13mo to\n56\t  cold-storage schema `observability.archive` (same table shape)\n57\t- `_archive/` Glacier transition: GitHub Actions monthly job packages `_archive/*.ts` → tarball → S3\n58\t  Glacier; index maintained in `docs/compliance/archive-index.md`\n59\t- Findings hash-chain: already implemented in `tools/gates/finding-registry.ts`; CI invariant\n60\t  `e2e/tests/integration/registry-hash-chain-intact.spec.ts` ships in Phase 5\n61\t\n62\t## Consequences\n63\t\n64\t**Positive**:\n65\t\n66\t- SOC2 Type II auditor walk-through: retention matrix is the single authoritative answer\n67\t- GDPR Art 5 defense: documented rationale for each retention ≥ minimum necessary\n68\t- Cross-tenant incidents: emergency_overrides 7y retention supports post-incident review\n69\t- Audit trail tamper-evidence: hash-chain + PII-scrub dual enforcement\n70\t\n71\t**Negative**:\n72\t\n73\t- Cold-storage automation (pg_cron + Glacier transition + git-LFS) is additional infra to maintain\n74\t- Separate retention per table means migrations must declare retention explicitly going forward\n75\t- PII-scrub false-positives may block legitimate finding entries — mitigated by explicit whitelist\n76\t  exceptions\n77\t\n78\t## Alternatives Considered\n79\t\n80\t1. **Uniform 7-year retention for everything**: simplicity, but violates GDPR minimisation for\n81\t   snapshots + operational data\n82\t2. **Uniform 90-day retention**: simplicity, but disqualifies SOC2 change-mgmt evidence\n83\t3. **External retention-management tool (AWS Macie, Varonis)**: over-engineered for current scale;\n84\t   revisit at >1000 tenants\n85\t\n86\t## Validation\n87\t\n88\t- Unit: `tools/gates/__tests__/findings-pii-scan.spec.ts` — positive (leaking field → fail) +\n89\t  negative (redacted → pass)\n90\t- Integration: `e2e/tests/integration/retention-policy-active.spec.ts` — TimescaleDB policy exists\n91\t  per table; cron job configured\n92\t- Audit: compliance-expert primary; observability-expert (TimescaleDB retention mechanics);\n93\t  infra-expert (Glacier + git-LFS cost model)\n94\t- E2E: auditor walkthrough — \"show me all schema changes to PII columns in Q3 2026\" → SQL query\n95\t  against `schema_object_history` returns answer\n96\t\n97\t## Exit Criteria\n98\t\n99\t- Matrix published + linked from `docs/compliance/retention-matrix.md` (canonical reference)\n100\t- Each artifact's retention enforced via code (not docs)\n101\t- PII-scrub gate active on every PR touching `findings.jsonl`\n102\t- Quarterly review: compliance-expert re-reads matrix against current regulations\n103\t\n104\t## References\n105\t\n106\t- SOC2 Trust Services Criteria (TSC) — CC4.1 Monitoring, CC7.1 Detection\n107\t- GDPR Art 5(e) — storage limitation\n108\t- KVKK Art 7 — data retention\n109\t- NIST SP 800-88 — media sanitisation (for cold-storage eventual destruction)\n110\t"}]},"parent_tool_use_id":null,"session_id":"46dfd730-1994-4098-95c5-80b1c536a456","uuid":"a4b4ceb6-50b6-45d6-bc66-e22d0ce52043","timestamp":"2026-09-25T10:04:38.032Z","tool_use_result":{"type":"text","file":{"filePath":"/home/gharunner/actions-runner/_work/aquaculture_platform/aquaculture_platform/aria-worktrees/req-AIR-aria-consensus-arbiter-d9d9f6d2ce58/docs/adr/024-compliance-retention-matrix.md","content":"# ADR-024: Compliance Retention Matrix\n\n**Status**: Accepted (2026-09-05, ADR-0012 in `docs/recommendations/architectural-arbiter/`)\n— enforced by the single registry-driven `RetentionEnforcementService`; windows are\ndeclared entity-typed in each service's retention bootstrap module\n**Plan reference**: `docs/plans/2026-04-21-db-migrate-enterprise-refactor.md` §v3 R17\n**Related**: ADR-022 (HMAC pepper), ADR-023 (encrypted columns)\n\n## Context\n\nPlan v2 specified disparate retentions across migration-adjacent artifacts (90d for\n`migration_events`, 30d for `_archive/`, 30d for schema snapshots, unspecified for\n`schema_object_history`, unlimited for `findings.jsonl`). Compliance-expert audit (v3) flagged:\n\n- 90d for `migration_events` < SOC2 12-month minimum (CC4.1 change-management evidence)\n- 30d for `_archive/` disqualifying for SOC2 Type II audit window\n- Unspecified `schema_object_history` fails auditor \"show me PII column history\" question\n- Unlimited `findings.jsonl` without PII-scrub gate risks Art 5(e) minimisation concern\n\nGDPR Art 5 (data minimisation — retention only as long as necessary) and SOC2 CC4.1\n(change-management evidence — typically 12mo+) create competing pressure. Without a principled\npolicy, retentions drift per-table without traceability.\n\n## Decision\n\nPublished retention matrix with dual-column (GDPR max, SOC2 min) and resolution logic.\n\n| Artifact                                                    | GDPR-max                             | SOC2-min                            | **DECISION**                              | Rationale                                                                                                         |\n| ----------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------ | ----------------------------------- | ----------------------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |\n| `observability.migration_events`                            | as short as necessary                | ≥ 12mo                              | **13 months**                             | SOC2 window + 1-month buffer; no PII after HMAC + erasure cascade (ADR-022); partition monthly                    |\n| `observability.schema_object_history`                       | no PII by design (column names only) | ≥ 12mo, 7y for change-mgmt          | **7 years**                               | Full SOC2 change-mgmt horizon; PII-scrubber CI gate asserts no tenant-identifier strings slip into old/new values |\n| `observability.emergency_overrides` (Phase 8 `aqua-ctl`)    | n/a                                  | ≥ 7 years (CC7.1 incident evidence) | **7 years**                               | Emergency override is incident-class; quarterly SRE review                                                        |\n| `apps/*/src/database/migrations/_archive/`                  | n/a                                  | ≥ 7 years                           | **7 years**                               | git-LFS + S3 Glacier (cost-effective cold storage); not in live filesystem                                        |\n| `s3://aqua-deploy-artifacts-fra1/schema-snapshots/`         | minimise (PII via column names)      | n/a                                 | **30 days**                               | Snapshot is deploy-gate input only; KVKK residency at FRA1 (ADR-024 cross-references R4 of plan)                  |\n| `docs/reviews/_registry/findings.jsonl`                     | minimise                             | ≥ 7 years (audit trail)             | **7 years + hash-chain + PII-scrub gate** | Append-only; cryptographic integrity; CI gate prevents PII leakage into audit log                                 |\n| `observability.migration_backfill_progress` (Phase 3.5)     | minimise                             | n/a                                 | **90 days after backfill completes**      | Operational/resumability data; stale rows serve no purpose                                                        |\n| `s3://aqua-deploy-artifacts-fra1/spaces-access-logs/` (R36) | minimise                             | n/a                                 | **1 year**                                | Forensics window for snapshot access                                                                              |\n\n### PII-scrubber gate for `findings.jsonl`\n\n`tools/gates/findings-pii-scan.ts` — CI gate scans every new registry entry for:\n\n- Email address regex\n- Phone number regex (E.164 + Turkish formats)\n- Turkish TC Kimlik No regex (11-digit validation algorithm)\n- IBAN regex\n- Credit card (PAN) regex\n\nOn match: PR fails with pointer to the leaking field; author must redact or use HMAC reference.\n\n### Implementation notes\n\n- `migration_events` partitioning: monthly via TimescaleDB retention policy `SELECT\nadd_retention_policy('migration_events', INTERVAL '13 months')`\n- `schema_object_history` 7y retention: pg_cron job monthly moves rows older than 13mo to\n  cold-storage schema `observability.archive` (same table shape)\n- `_archive/` Glacier transition: GitHub Actions monthly job packages `_archive/*.ts` → tarball → S3\n  Glacier; index maintained in `docs/compliance/archive-index.md`\n- Findings hash-chain: already implemented in `tools/gates/finding-registry.ts`; CI invariant\n  `e2e/tests/integration/registry-hash-chain-intact.spec.ts` ships in Phase 5\n\n## Consequences\n\n**Positive**:\n\n- SOC2 Type II auditor walk-through: retention matrix is the single authoritative answer\n- GDPR Art 5 defense: documented rationale for each retention ≥ minimum necessary\n- Cross-tenant incidents: emergency_overrides 7y retention supports post-incident review\n- Audit trail tamper-evidence: hash-chain + PII-scrub dual enforcement\n\n**Negative**:\n\n- Cold-storage automation (pg_cron + Glacier transition + git-LFS) is additional infra to maintain\n- Separate retention per table means migrations must declare retention explicitly going forward\n- PII-scrub false-positives may block legitimate finding entries — mitigated by explicit whitelist\n  exceptions\n\n## Alternatives Considered\n\n1. **Uniform 7-year retention for everything**: simplicity, but violates GDPR minimisation for\n   snapshots + operational data\n2. **Uniform 90-day retention**: simplicity, but disqualifies SOC2 change-mgmt evidence\n3. **External retention-management tool (AWS Macie, Varonis)**: over-engineered for current scale;\n   revisit at >1000 tenants\n\n## Validation\n\n- Unit: `tools/gates/__tests__/findings-pii-scan.spec.ts` — positive (leaking field → fail) +\n  negative (redacted → pass)\n- Integration: `e2e/tests/integration/retention-policy-active.spec.ts` — TimescaleDB policy exists\n  per table; {"type":"user","message":{"role":"user","content":[{"tool_use_id":"toolu_0185MvXTUJbnCyU7dyCzxhyo","type":"tool_result","content":"1\t# Retention Matrix — Authoritative per-table retention policy\n2\t\n3\t**Closes:** [COMPLIANCE-HIGH-007](../reviews/compliance-expert/2026-04-28-core-platform-review.md#COMPLIANCE-HIGH-007)\n4\t\n5\t**Status:** AUTHORITATIVE STRUCTURE. The retention-days values\n6\tbelow are derived from [ADR-024](../adr/024-compliance-retention-matrix.md)\n7\tand the canonical TypeScript registry at\n8\t`libs/backend-common/src/database/retention/retention-policy.ts`.\n9\tThe TypeScript registry is the runtime source of truth — this\n10\tmarkdown file is the human-readable mirror referenced by\n11\tKVKK / GDPR / SOC 2 audits.\n12\t\n13\tWhen the two diverge, the canonical TypeScript registry wins; an\n14\tinvariant test (planned per COMPLIANCE-HIGH-007 follow-on) will\n15\tensure the markdown rows stay in lockstep with the registry.\n16\t\n17\t---\n18\t\n19\t## How retention durations are derived\n20\t\n21\t| Source of truth | Authority |\n22\t|---|---|\n23\t| TypeScript registry — `RetentionPolicy.retentionDays` per service-owned `registerRetentionPolicy()` call | Runtime enforcement (ADR-024) |\n24\t| ADR-024 §3 floor table | Per-domain minimum |\n25\t| GDPR Art 5(1)(e) — storage limitation | Outer ceiling for personal data |\n26\t| KVKK Art 7 — destruction obligation | Outer ceiling for personal data |\n27\t| Sectoral statutes (İş Kanunu, VUK, Türk Ticaret Kanunu) | Floor for HR + financial domains |\n28\t| SOC 2 CC4.1 (audit-log integrity) | Floor for audit / change-management |\n29\t\n30\tWhen sectoral floor (e.g. İş Kanunu 10y) is higher than GDPR\n31\tceiling (5y), the floor wins. Each row's `legal_basis` column\n32\tdocuments which authority dominates.\n33\t\n34\t---\n35\t\n36\t## Retention table — by schema + table\n37\t\n38\t| Schema | Table | Retention (days) | Years | Legal basis | Destruction method | Service owner |\n39\t|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|\n40\t| `auth` | `users` | 365 after account close | 1y | KVKK Art 7 + GDPR Art 17 | DELETE (cascade) | auth-service |"}]},"parent_tool_use_id":null,"session_id":"46dfd730-1994-4098-95c5-80b1c536a456","uuid":"a3f6285c-175c-42ba-9bd7-ceccd859ec88","timestamp":"2026-09-25T10:05:38.459Z","tool_use_result":{"type":"text","file":{"filePath":"/home/gharunner/actions-runner/_work/aquaculture_platform/aquaculture_platform/aria-worktrees/req-AIR-aria-consensus-arbiter-d9d9f6d2ce58/docs/compliance/retention-matrix.md","content":"# Retention Matrix — Authoritative per-table retention policy\n\n**Closes:** [COMPLIANCE-HIGH-007](../reviews/compliance-expert/2026-04-28-core-platform-review.md#COMPLIANCE-HIGH-007)\n\n**Status:** AUTHORITATIVE STRUCTURE. The retention-days values\nbelow are derived from [ADR-024](../adr/024-compliance-retention-matrix.md)\nand the canonical TypeScript registry at\n`libs/backend-common/src/database/retention/retention-policy.ts`.\nThe TypeScript registry is the runtime source of truth — this\nmarkdown file is the human-readable mirror referenced by\nKVKK / GDPR / SOC 2 audits.\n\nWhen the two diverge, the canonical TypeScript registry wins; an\ninvariant test (planned per COMPLIANCE-HIGH-007 follow-on) will\nensure the markdown rows stay in lockstep with the registry.\n\n---\n\n## How retention durations are derived\n\n| Source of truth | Authority |\n|---|---|\n| TypeScript registry — `RetentionPolicy.retentionDays` per service-owned `registerRetentionPolicy()` call | Runtime enforcement (ADR-024) |\n| ADR-024 §3 floor table | Per-domain minimum |\n| GDPR Art 5(1)(e) — storage limitation | Outer ceiling for personal data |\n| KVKK Art 7 — destruction obligation | Outer ceiling for personal data |\n| Sectoral statutes (İş Kanunu, VUK, Türk Ticaret Kanunu) | Floor for HR + financial domains |\n| SOC 2 CC4.1 (audit-log integrity) | Floor for audit / change-management |\n\nWhen sectoral floor (e.g. İş Kanunu 10y) is higher than GDPR\nceiling (5y), the floor wins. Each row's `legal_basis` column\ndocuments which authority dominates.\n\n---\n\n## Retention table — by schema + table\n\n| Schema | Table | Retention (days) | Years | Legal basis | Destruction method | Service owner |\n|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|\n| `auth` | `users` | 365 after account close | 1y | KVKK Art 7 + GDPR Art 17 | DELETE (cascade) | auth-service |","numLines":40,"startLine":1,"totalLines":172}}}
